seo.title: MyReciBook — Rescue the recipes buried in your camera roll
seo.description: MyReciBook turns recipe screenshots, links and handwritten cards into a cookbook you own. Plain files on your phone. Pay once. Cook forever. Android.

recipe.title: A cookbook you own
ingredients: a pinch of patience while it reads cursive
steps: Share a screenshot, paste a link, or snap grandma's card with the camera.
The AI turns it into a proper recipe — ingredients, steps and timings — and shows you the result to review before it's saved.
File it in your book. It lives on your phone; export a PDF or document whenever you like.
recipe.spineNote: AI is remarkably good in scanning texts and images

cookMode.title: Cook mode
cookMode.body: One step at a time in big, kitchen-proof type. Tap zones sized for floury thumbs, timers built in.

grocery.title: Grocery list
grocery.body: “9 items · from 3 planned recipes” — merged, deduplicated, and it asks before combining 2 lemons with 4.

pantry.title: Pantry
pantry.body: Know what's on the shelf. Categories fold away, recents float up, and the grocery list checks against it.

diary.title: Food diary
diary.body: Log meals straight from your recipes and pantry — no double typing. Trends show your week without the guilt trip.

barcode.title: Barcode scanner
barcode.body: Point it at the package. Open Food Facts fills in the product and its nutrition — most countries covered.

nutrition.title: Nutrition tracking
nutrition.body: Energy, macros and micros per day, week and year — with coverage you can actually see, not just totals.

pocket.title: The box, in your pocket.
pocket.lede: Coverless recipes get a hand-me-down gradient cover, picked by the title so it never changes. Search, filters and your shelves — one thumb, one screen.
pocket.pointBarcode: Barcode scanner with Open Food Facts behind it — most countries covered
pocket.pointTrends: Nutrition trends by day, week and year — no guilt trip
pocket.pointTheme: Stitch Slate by day, Midnight by night

yours.title:
If MyReciBook vanished tomorrow,
your recipes wouldn't, unless...
yours.lede:
So your cookbook lives on your phone — not on someone else's cloud server. But you can back it up to your Drive, Dropbox and export any recipe as a PDF or other formats.
That way if you drop your phone into a volcano, your data is saved. :)
